topic: Harness² (harness2): Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World (Google Cloud AI Research + Northwestern University)

claims.claim: A harness is the system around a model that lets it act as an agent: prompts, tools, memory, skills, orchestration. 'Harnessing' is optimizing that system. README: "A harness is the system around a model that enables it to act as an agent: prompts, tools, memory, skills, orchestration, and more."

sources.title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World

claims.claim: Improves agents while keeping model weights fixed. README: "It connects two levels of recursion while keeping model weights fixed". Paper: harnessing = "optimizing the runtime scaffolding around a frozen base model"; "Model weights, stage instructions, and the decision rule remain fixed, while the library evolves."

Eight editable harness components, each mounted as a file: system prompt, guardrails, memory, tool guidance, subagents, skills, scripts, and plugins (middleware plugin). Extends AHE's file-level decomposition by one component.

Task-level recursion: a contrastive Propose–Probe–Compose step. Run the current harness once as a reference; PROPOSE two candidate edits (an 'invariant' candidate for general agent weaknesses like planning, tool use, context, delegation; a 'domain-specific' candidate for the task's domain knowledge/procedures); PROBE: run each candidate on the same task under matched conditions and compare behaviour with the reference (a 'behavioral contrast'); COMPOSE: merge supported changes, revise conflicts, adopt one, or keep the current harness, then run the composed harness. No ground-truth answers are used. README: "propose edits, probe their effects on the same task, and compose a refined harness from behavioral contrasts between executions, without ground-truth feedback."

Budget k scales the step. Parallel: probe k invariant + k domain candidates, produce k compositions, then an agentic selector picks the best anonymized deliverable. Sequential: chain k Propose–Probe–Compose steps. At k=1 both reduce to one step. README: "Parallel recursion explores wider; sequential recursion refines deeper."

Harnessing-level recursion: after each task an experience reflector reviews the whole improvement record and saves the adopted harness plus evidence-supported lessons into a 'harness improvement library' (each entry = executable harness + EXPERIENCE.md). The next task starts from the same base harness, but proposals can reuse/adapt library entries. Paper: "Lessons are retained only when supported by execution contrasts".

A single step (k=1) improves GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base harnesses in all four model–harness configs (OpenCode, Codex). Max gains: +11.5 points WorkBuddy-Bench (GLM-5/OpenCode, 64.2 -> 75.7 avg), +4.5 points JobBench (Gemini 3.5 Flash/OpenCode, 31.5 -> 36.0), +11.8 percentage points LAB Partial pass rate (GLM-5/OpenCode, 59.6 -> 71.4). Means over three runs.

Parallel recursion at k=5 adds a further 2.9-3.9 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 3.0-4.2 on JobBench, 2.6-6.7 pp on LAB Partial over a single step. Gemini 3.5 Flash/OpenCode WorkBuddy avg: base 72.4 -> k=1 77.5 (+5.1) -> k=5 80.8 (+8.4 total). JobBench same config: +4.5 at k=1 to +7.5 at k=5.

With one step, GLM-5 reaches 75.7 (OpenCode) and 75.3 (Codex) on WorkBuddy-Bench, above base Gemini 3.5 Flash's 72.4 and 74.5. Paper: "A weaker model with an improved harness can thus outperform a stronger one with its original harness."

Frozen executors: Gemini 3.5 Flash and GLM-5 under OpenCode and Codex harnesses. Default harness editor: Claude Opus 4.8 under OpenCode. Library starts empty per benchmark stream. Same-model-as-editor test (k=2): all five models improve; GLM-5 +13.7 on LAB, Claude Opus 5 +3.3/+5.5/+3.0.

JobBench case study (Gemini 3.5 Flash, OpenCode): one task's score rose from 43.1 to 77.8 after an invariant guardrail (inventory inputs, trace figures, re-open and verify output files) and a domain skill for reconciling schedule/venue/labor/budget files.

Code licensed Apache 2.0 (third-party code, benchmarks and datasets keep upstream licenses). Paper licensed CC BY 4.0. Repo created 2026-10-06, initial public commit 2026-10-08, arXiv v1 submitted 2026-10-09, package version 0.1.0, Python >=3.12,<3.14. README: "This is not an officially supported Google product."

Authors: Ruiyao Xu (Northwestern University), Yanfei Chen, Zhongying CuiZhu, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Yifei Ming, Han Yu, Rujun Han, Chen-Yu Lee, Tomas Pfister (Google Cloud AI Research). Hosted under the google-research GitHub org; the paper's affiliation is Google Cloud AI Research, not 'Google Research' as such.

Install/run: `uv venv --python 3.12 .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && uv pip install -e '.[render]'`; credential-free demo `harness2-demo --output runs/demo --k 2`; benchmark e.g. `harness2-setup jb` then `harness2 --bench jb --k 1 --mode parallel`; also `harness2-judge` and `harness2-report`. `--substrate cx` uses Codex. Requires Linux; model runs need Node.js 20+, Google Cloud CLI, Vertex AI.

Authors' limitations: extra executions and editor sessions add inference cost as budget grows (parallelism cuts latency, not compute); feedback is behavioural contrast plus model judgment, sensitive to run-to-run variability and shared model biases, and does "not guarantee correctness or establish that an adopted change will transfer to a different task." README: model-backed runs incur API costs; executor network is unrestricted and Codex runs with sandbox disabled; public benchmark rubrics may be online, so restrict network before evaluating. Results are benchmark evaluations (3 runs each), not production deployments. Recursion does not uniformly close gaps between harnesses; on LAB Partial, Meta-Harness leads for Gemini 3.5 Flash/Codex.
